matches.rationale: No finding addresses the Abstract; all findings target specific sections (Section 3.3, Tables 1/3, Appendix E). The claim that the abstract exaggerates generalizability by omitting dataset limitations is not identified.

The Method section issue about glossing over tensor-product operator complexity is not captured by any finding. Finding 1 addresses an undefined M^H in Section 3.3, and Finding 5 targets an Appendix proof, neither of which concerns the Representer theorem derivation shortcut.

No finding discusses the delta hyperparameter search protocol or its selective tuning across datasets. The findings identify numerical/claim errors in Table 1, not experimental design fairness regarding hyperparameter selection.

Finding pred_id=3 shows that Section 4.2's claims of OGL²P+JMMD-HSIC superiority directly contradict the Table 1 data (it is worse than OGL²P and RSDA-MSTN). This captures the same underlying evidence-data-integrity issue: the paper inflates the impression of average superiority by making unsupported claims about the same table, even though the specific mechanism (cherry-picking vs. false in-text claims) is described differently.

The ground truth criticizes Table 3 for lacking error bars and statistical significance on minimal accuracy differences. Finding pred_id=4 notes a numerical conflict between Table 1 and Table 3 but does not mention missing variance or significance reporting in Table 3.
The fabrication of the ImageCLEF-DA dataset is not mentioned in any finding. All findings focus on methodological or numerical issues within standard benchmark tables and derivations.
No finding discusses the absence of ethical/fairness considerations or bias disclosures in the experimental datasets section. This topic is entirely unaddressed by the findings list.

The Conclusion's promotional and exaggerated language is not identified by any finding. The findings are restricted to methodology, table numbers, and proof details, not rhetorical presentation in the conclusion.

The incoherence between the Method section's complementarity claims and variable experimental outcomes (JMMD alone matching/exceeding the combined model) is not identified. The findings do not address this method-to-experiment narrative mismatch.
No finding discusses whether baseline methods and JMMD-HSIC share identical feature extractors (SURF, DECAF-6, ResNet-50) or training setups. This fairness concern is not raised.
The selective use of dashed boxes in Figure 2 to highlight favorable distribution alignments while omitting unfavorable regions is not mentioned in any finding.
The Introduction's exaggerated characterization of Wasserstein distance as inconvenient for subspace learning is not identified by any finding.
Tables 6 and 7 are not mentioned in any finding. The lack of variance/confidence intervals and rounding issues in these specific tables are therefore unaddressed.
No finding identifies fabricated citations with unrealistic publication years and volume/page numbers in the References section.
The omission of a conflict-of-interest declaration in the acknowledgments/appendix is not raised by any finding.
